items.claim: The rejected-alternative sentence names another unit by its position rather than by verse, a register violation, though the seam itself is byte-warranted and independently corroborated by the neighboring unit's own closing claim.
items.evidence: strongest_rejected_alternative states the two wish-cries are "kept together as the row before this one" -- a positional reference to another unit by its position, which the standing register rule bars from row prose in favor of verse-anchored cross-references. The underlying seam is otherwise sound: oshb:Jer.9.2 (= web:Jer.9.3) opens a fresh main clause in third-person description ("vayadrekhu et leshonam qashtam sheqer") after the wish-formula's own subordinate "ki" (because) clause closes at web:Jer.9.2 (= oshb:Jer.9.1), and the neighboring unit's own boundary claim independently closes at that same seam. The setumah marks disclosed at oshb:Jer.9.2 and oshb:Jer.9.5 (= web:Jer.9.6) are correctly typed against the parashah inventory.

items.claim: The unit's koh-amar-tsevaot onset and its closing shift into a fresh disputation question are both byte-warranted and mutually corroborated by the adjacent units' own boundary claims.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.9.6 (= web:Jer.9.7) opens with the full "koh amar YHWH tsevaot" formula immediately after the neum-YHWH close of the preceding material, and oshb:Jer.9.10 (= web:Jer.9.11) closes on the judgment verdict before oshb:Jer.9.11 (= web:Jer.9.12) turns to an unformulaic rhetorical question; both edges match the adjacent units' own independently stated boundaries. The zone ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.9.7 (= web:Jer.9.8) is correctly disclosed as the offset zone's one ketiv/qere verse (book-wide ketiv/qere inventory: 141 notes over 124 verses, exactly one sited inside the zone), and the setumot cited at oshb:Jer.9.5, oshb:Jer.9.8, and oshb:Jer.9.10 are correctly typed against the parashah inventory.

items.claim: The prose disputation is correctly bounded at its register shift into and out of poetry, and its disclosed tension between a disputation shape and a judgment_oracle type is honestly resolved on the verdict it shares with its neighbors.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.9.11 (= web:Jer.9.12) opens on an unformulaic question set in prose while the material on both sides carries WEB poetry-line formatting (texture only, not the seam's driver), and the unit correctly declines to cut a fresh row at the "lachen koh amar YHWH tsevaot Elohei Yisrael" clause at oshb:Jer.9.14 (= web:Jer.9.15) because "lachen" (therefore) ties it grammatically to the diagnosis opening at oshb:Jer.9.12 (= web:Jer.9.13) rather than beginning an unrelated address -- a real rival, correctly rejected on the bytes rather than by reflex koh-amar cutting. The petuchah at oshb:Jer.9.15 (= web:Jer.9.16) and the setumot at oshb:Jer.9.10, oshb:Jer.9.11, and oshb:Jer.9.13 are correctly typed against the inventory.

items.claim: The mourning-women summons is a well-bounded unit whose closing formula is correctly disclosed as a variant construction distinct from the book's standard koh-amar-YHWH shape.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.9.16 (= web:Jer.9.17) opens the standard "koh amar YHWH tsevaot" formula paired with a plural summoning imperative, and the unit correctly names the closing shape at oshb:Jer.9.21 (= web:Jer.9.22) -- "dabber koh ne'um YHWH" -- as pairing the bare imperative "speak" with "ne'um YHWH" rather than the book's usual "koh amar YHWH," disclosing it apart from the koh-amar-YHWH census rather than folding it in as an ordinary instance (a real hazard: a bare koh-token sweep would misclassify this site). The petuchah at oshb:Jer.9.15 and the setumot at oshb:Jer.9.18 and oshb:Jer.9.21 are correctly typed against the inventory, and the unit correctly closes before the standard-shape koh-amar onset at oshb:Jer.9.22 (= web:Jer.9.23).

items.claim: The wisdom-saying unit is tightly bounded by a standard koh-amar onset and a neum-YHWH close, and its judgment_oracle typing over disputed wisdom-saying content is honestly disclosed as a controlled-vocabulary stand-in.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.9.22 (= web:Jer.9.23) opens an unbridged "koh amar YHWH" onset turning from the mourning summons to a boasting saying, and closes at oshb:Jer.9.23 (= web:Jer.9.24) on its own neum-YHWH tag immediately before "hinneh yamim ba'im, ne'um YHWH" opens fresh matter at oshb:Jer.9.24 (= web:Jer.9.25) -- the same recurring shape accurately cross-referenced to web:Jer.7.32. The setumot at oshb:Jer.9.21 and oshb:Jer.9.23 are correctly typed against the inventory.

items.claim: The boundary_rationale field names the production plan's own segmentation of the book alongside the unit's own edge, a register violation, though the unit's formula-driven boundaries and its nations-list disclosure are otherwise sound.
items.evidence: boundary_rationale's closing sentence reads "the row and the part both end at 9.26" (web:Jer.9.26 = oshb:Jer.9.25) -- naming the writer's own administrative division of the book rather than a textual fact, which the standing register rule bars as a cross-part reference in any field. The underlying boundary is nonetheless byte-warranted: oshb:Jer.9.24 (= web:Jer.9.25) opens on "hinneh yamim ba'im, ne'um YHWH," the same recurring formula accurately cross-referenced to web:Jer.7.32, and the roster-plus-verdict at oshb:Jer.9.25 (= web:Jer.9.26) is one grammatical sentence -- a "ki" (for) clause ties the uncircumcised-nations verdict to the roster -- correctly kept as one unit rather than split at the list-to-verdict turn; device_notes correctly distinguish this rhetorical nation list from the header-bounded nations_oracle material later in the book. The setumot at oshb:Jer.9.23 and oshb:Jer.9.25 are correctly typed against the inventory.

items.claim: The idol-polemic-through-Aramaic-citation unit correctly declines to split its mockery/praise alternation absent a tier-1 marker and correctly discloses the Aramaic island inside its own span.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.10.1 opens the discourse-frame imperative "hear the word," and oshb:Jer.10.2 follows at once with a koh-amar onset; between that onset and the close at oshb:Jer.10.11, no fresh koh-amar, addressee shift, or discourse imperative marks a seam, so the doxological second-person praise at oshb:Jer.10.6-Jer.10.7 is correctly held inside the same divine speech as the surrounding idol mockery rather than atomized on a theme-only basis. oshb:Jer.10.11 is Aramaic, the book's single attested Aramaic-language verse (morph-code sweep: 15 A-prefixed codes, all sited in this one verse), and device_notes correctly disclose the island as required for any span covering it. The setumot at oshb:Jer.10.5, oshb:Jer.10.10, and oshb:Jer.10.11 are correctly typed against the inventory and correctly held as non-driving texture.

items.claim: The creation-doxology unit is correctly typed and its closing name-formula's link to the doxology's twin at Jer.51.15-Jer.51.19 is correctly disclosed as cross-book texture rather than as the boundary's own driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.10.12 opens a participial hymn shape immediately after the Aramaic close at oshb:Jer.10.11, matching the hymn_doxology type's own catalogued example, and closes at oshb:Jer.10.16 on the "YHWH tsevaot shemo" name-formula; the neighboring unit's own opening claim independently confirms the seam at oshb:Jer.10.16/oshb:Jer.10.17. The ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.10.13 holds at the byte level: the unpointed ketiv ארץ stands immediately before the pointed qere הָאָ֑רֶץ in the source bytes. The setumot at oshb:Jer.10.11 and oshb:Jer.10.16 are correctly typed against the inventory and correctly held as non-driving texture.
